This PR prevents anndata from warning so aggressively.

Description `PercentilePostprocessor` now takes the percentile over off-diagonal entries only, so the diagonal zeros of `dst` no longer lower the threshold. Graphs built with `percentile` change slightly.

`spatial_scatter` checked the image keys under `adata.uns[spatial_key]` but loaded images and scalefactors from `adata.uns["spatial"]`, so any other `spatial_key` failed. This loads images, scalefactors and segmentation images from `adata.uns[spatial_key]`, as the `library_id` docs describe.

`assign_stitch_groups` now stores its arguments under `uns["tiling_stitch"]["params"]`, so the re-run hint in `calculate_tiling_qc` prints them as is. This drops `_STITCH_PARAM_KEYS`, `_STITCH_COLUMNS` and the private imports into `_tiling_qc`.

`test_destvi_vamp_prior_from_normal_condscvi` (default and `"normal"` prior): trains DestVI and checks the proportions. - `test_destvi_qz_prior_follows_module`: after `module.double()`, `qz_prior` and its samples are float64. CI has no GPU, so this checks the same mechanism through dtype.
Trimmed port of #4017, plus the crash fix from #4018. Outputs are bit-identical before and after.

Part of #4240, without resolving it: on `main`, these timer chains multiply the scheduling rounds (10,195 instead of 397 for 400 jobs below), and each round repeats the scheduling work discussed there.
Use a rule's effective pathvars when creating default storage queries, including multiext prefixes, while keeping workflow defaults for callers without a rule context.

Declare `ggplot`, `ggplot_built`, `uneval`, and the four legacy element names in the S7 class hierarchy. Subclasses then inherit these compatibility names, which are currently added only by ggplot2's constructors.

Plot and theme addition currently reports `e2` in errors with development S7. Capture the original operand in the method so errors identify expressions such as `geom_point`, while retaining the existing capture path for S7 0.2.2.

Besides the warning, with `drop = FALSE` a named variable was returned as is instead of as an id, and `id()` over a named variable and another one errored in `vapply()`. Those now give the same ids as the unnamed variable.
